newsitem.title: USA: DAKA does not expect to meet expectations.
newsitem.headline: DAKA does not expect to meet expectations.

text.p: DAKA International said on Monday that it does not expect to meet analysts' expectations for fiscal 1997, and it expects lower estimates to a range of $0.70 to $0.80 per share.

The company said that an unfavorable impact on earnings for the third and fourth quarters of fiscal 1996 are projected to continue to adversely impact anticipated results for fiscal 1997, particularly in the first quarter which will be substantially below the first quarter results for fiscal 1996, and will most likely result in a net loss.
Daka said that the Fuddrucker's segment continues to be disappointing for the first two months of the new fiscal year.

The company's negotiations for the proposed Kmart Corp joint venture have not been completed delaying the closing of the transaction. Daka continues to incur costs associated with this proposed joint venture, it said.
The Champps segment continues to experience poor operating margins based on costs associated with the new restaurants including amortization of pre-opening expenses.
The company said it intents to intensely focus on the core businesses and improve their profitability to acceptable levels.

DAKA added that it is confident of its strategic direction and although it will take some time to return to acceptable quarterly performance, its opportunities for growth and profitability remain strong.
